thread:
mira: Post-RFC checkin: I'm proposing a two-step connector onboarding pattern to reduce blast radius for Private customers. Step A = "hello" (minimal attestation + connectivity hint). Step B = "bind" (upgrade to full dataplane).

mira: Hello should be tiny: tenant_id, proof_sig (kms-signed or short CP token), ip_hint (could be private/local), optional ipv6_hint, and feature_flags list. No long polling or KV yet.

sam: Nice. How does the bind get authorized without redoing an expensive KMS op?

kevin: bind should reference the hello thumbprint + present a fresh ephemeral key signed by connector's local cert. CP verifies thumbprint -> issues bind session token (long TTL). This avoids another tenant KMS signature.

mira: Example HELLO payload:```
POST /connect/hello HTTP/1.1
Host: cp.redwood.internal
X-Connector-Features: hello,ipv6
{
  "tenant":"T-201",
  "proof":"sig:kms:v2:abc...",
  "ip_hint":"192.168.10.4",
  "ipv6_hint":"fd00::4"
}
```

dan: If cp issues bind token, we need a clear revocation path. For enterprise, tenant may rotate KMS or kill connector. CP should accept revocation list and short revocation TTL for bind tokens.

kevin: also need to define where TLS terminates in Step B: for Private keep end-to-end to connector; for Hosted we may TLS-terminate at the regional relay with mTLS back to connector. That means bind token semantics slightly differ depending on deployment mode.

mira: agreed. We'll encode deployment_mode in hello: "mode":"private|dedicated|hosted" so CP can decide termination and token format.

sam: edge case: overlapping CIDRs across tenants in same VPC -> ip_hint may be ambiguous. We should allow source-port_hint and a NAT-hairpin flag so connector can request an assumed public egress IP mapping.

mira: good call. Add fields: nat_mapping_hint, hairpin_ok(true/false).

ops-bot: :information_source: perf-test job scheduled: nat-hairpin-sim -> infra-test-9 (results ETA 2h)

dan: migration plan: 1) support hello-only endpoints in CP and keep legacy behavior; 2) release connector v2 with optional bind step; 3) canary bind for 3 tenants (non-critical) for 48h; 4) gradual opt-in at tenant flag. Fallback: if bind fails, connector remains hello-only and proxies via regional-relay.

kevin: add a compatibility header so CP can reply with `X-CP-Suggest: bind-delay=300` if CP needs time before accepting binds. That avoids flapping.

mira: Ops/alerts: track hello_success_rate, bind_success_rate, bind_latency_p95, bind_revoked_count, nat_mismatch_rate. Create incident trigger if bind_revoked_count spikes > 5 in 1h.

sam: logging: include hello.trace_id forwarded to bind for cross-correlation. Also surface clear error codes: `HB_401_BAD_PROOF`, `HB_426_BIND_REQUIRED`, `HB_409_FEATURE_MISMATCH`. That will make triage way faster.

dan: question on kv-sync: if connector doesn't support kv-sync on bind, CP should return `feature_x_required` with a human URL and connector should fallback to poll-mode. Avoid timeouts by returning `expected_retry_after` header.

kevin: IPv6 note: some on-prem NATs rewrite addresses; bind must support a confirmation handshake where CP returns observed_source and connector compares to ip_hint and nat_mapping_hint. If mismatch and hairpin_ok=false, CP rejects bind.

ops-bot: :gear: started canary deploy and smoke tests for bind protocol (canary id: 374555-canary-2). Logs: https://deploys.internal/redwood/3745556666

mira: docs: I'll add a concise protocol appendix with JSON schemata for hello and bind, sample headers, error codes, and suggested retries. Also a runbook: how to roll back per-tenant flag, and how to patch revocation list quickly.

sam: timeline: can review appendix today, prototype connector changes tomorrow, ops runbook by Friday.

kevin: one more ops wrinkle: ensure metrics exported to tenant-specific dashboards for the canary tenants so SRE can watch egress ip preservation.

mira: ok. I'll open a short follow-up thread with the appendix link and set the tenant-flag checklist. Thanks all.
